clue.text: Is it rolled tar or asphalt?

definitions.meaning: a cricket playing surface is flattened with a heavy roller before a match
a black sticky road-surfacing substance distilled from tar

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the strip between the wickets is rolled before play; the page prints 'turgor' where the clue needs 'tar or'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket ground's strip is rolled flat, and the same word names the black resin used like tar for surfacing.

clue.text: Tempestuous duke to get on with an appeal

parts.note: to get on in life is to thrive or do well
O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O help me'

explanation.surface: A stormy nobleman tries to advance himself by pleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tempestuous duke' means the duke from Shakespeare's play The Tempest, not an angry one.
explanation.definitionFit: The deposed Duke of Milan is the magician hero of Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Applicants hope it will bring news of what they have applied for

definitions.text: Applicants hope it will bring news of what they have applied for

parts.words: Applicants hope it will bring news of what they have applied for
parts.note: job seekers wait for the morning delivery of letters to learn whether they got the job

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a newspaper, but the news comes in the mail delivery; 'applied for' hints at the job sense of 'post'.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters delivered each morning carry offers or rejections to job candidates.

clue.text: Pop or wine?

definitions.meaning: to pop something is slang for pawning it
a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.definitionFit: To pawn goods is slang 'pop', and German Rhine whites are sold under this name.

clue.text: Furious herald would call it rampant

definitions.meaning: very angry and protesting
in heraldry a rampant beast rears up with its forelegs raised

explanation.walkthrough: A herald here is an expert in coats of arms, where 'rampant' describes an animal standing on its hind legs with forelegs aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is idiomatically described this way, and a heraldic rampant lion literally rears with raised forelimbs.

clue.text: East European of renown gets Capone to eat heartily

parts.note: someone or something from Poland is Polish
renown means fame
Al Capone was the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A famous Pole teams up with a gangster for a big dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing a dinner quickly and completely is the idiom for devouring it.

clue.text: Not one could name one

explanation.surface: Nobody could put a name to a single one.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun meaning nobody or not any.

clue.text: Colour spectrum described by eminent London artist?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an eminent artist
a thing described by a place is located in it, so these words give a short word of position
Bow is a district of East London

explanation.surface: A range of colours painted by a distinguished London painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'an RA in Bow': a Royal Academician living in Bow, an East London district.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc of separated colours seen when sunlight passes through rain is the spectrum in the sky.

clue.text: Tourist attraction in a sense

definitions.meaning: a notable place that visitors go to see
vision, one of the five senses

explanation.definitionFit: Places visitors see are 'the sights', and vision is one of the five senses.

clue.text: They won't go out to meet big waves

definitions.meaning: workers who refuse to join an industrial walkout
to hit large breaking waves at sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out' means go on strike; read the second part as 'strike' (meet) plus 'breakers' (big waves).
explanation.definitionFit: Scabs who keep working are called this, and literally the phrase means hitting surf.

clue.text: Mine needs bandaging

definitions.meaning: a surface mine worked from the top without shafts
describes an unhealed wound in the skin

explanation.definitionFit: Surface quarrying is called open-cast or open-cut mining, and an unhealed gash calls for a dressing.

clue.text: The end of a flight at the top of the flight

definitions.meaning: an aircraft's touchdown at the end of a journey

definitions.text: at the top of the flight
definitions.meaning: the platform at the head of a flight of stairs

explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's touchdown and the floor space at the head of a staircase share this word.

clue.text: Support not required by a jet plane

definitions.meaning: something that holds another up

definitions.text: not required by a jet plane
definitions.meaning: short for propeller, which jet engines do without

explanation.definitionFit: A prop holds something up, and it is also the short form for an aircraft propeller, which jets lack.

clue.text: Small investment in valuable fur produces capital for Belarus

indicators.note: an investment is something put in, so the small letter is placed inside the fur

parts.note: mink is a prized fur
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A modest stake in a pricey fur coat earns money for Belarus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment in' looks financial, but it signals putting S inside MINK; 'capital' is the city, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: The city that is the seat of Belarus's government.

clue.text: A wager to help criminal activity

parts.note: a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: Someone places a bet to back a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist or encourage wrongdoing, as in 'aid and abet'.

clue.text: Honours for the winner of the race

definitions.meaning: a top-class university honours degree
the one who comes in ahead of everyone

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'first' is the top class of honours degree.
explanation.definitionFit: British universities award top-class honours degrees under this name, and a race winner comes in ahead.

clue.text: Poles are to set a trap

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles

explanation.surface: Polish people are setting a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland but gives the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch an animal in a noose or snare is to trap it.

clue.text: Paper shop proprietor who passes on gossip

definitions.meaning: a newsagent, who sells newspapers
a person who spreads stories

explanation.definitionFit: A newsagent sells papers, and a gossip spreads stories, so both trade in tidings.

clue.text: Recalcitrance of French boy friend

parts.note: de is French for of
a fiance is a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's boyfriend is being stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn refusal to obey is open resistance.

clue.text: Text book example of an angry allusion

parts.note: cross means angry
an allusion is a reference

explanation.surface: A textbook shows an instance of an irate hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A note directing the reader to another passage of the same text is a standard feature of books.

clue.text: British sappers and American soldiers need discipline

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's sappers
GI men are US soldiers

explanation.surface: British engineers and US troops require order.
explanation.definitionFit: A prescribed course of diet or exercise is a strict regime.

clue.text: Intoxicating drink derived from gentian

indicators.note: derived from says the drink's letters come out of the plant name, reworked

explanation.surface: A heady liquor is distilled from a gentian plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derived from' rearranges GENTIAN; gentian root really flavours some spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Undiluted spirit, served straight, is strong liquor.

clue.text: Menial schoolboys were forbidden them

definitions.meaning: junior boys at English public schools who served seniors
cigarettes, which schoolboys were not allowed

explanation.walkthrough: At old British boarding schools, juniors did chores for older pupils; the same word is British slang for cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Juniors who did chores for older boys at British public schools bore this name, which is also slang for cigarettes.

clue.text: Flying Officer leading weird discussion group

indicators.note: leading puts the officer's letters in front of the next piece

parts.note: FO is the RAF abbreviation for Flying Officer
rum means odd or weird

explanation.surface: An RAF officer heads up a strange debating society.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting or medium for open debate, from the Roman public square.

clue.text: Foolish enough to give second-rate service

parts.note: B grade is second-rate
the army is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Being silly is enough to provide poor service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like waiting at table, but means an armed service.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for crazy or daft.

clue.text: Name "The Greatest" country in Africa

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for name
boxer Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

explanation.surface: Naming the greatest nation in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlocked West African state whose capital is Bamako.

clue.text: Did it chew up the fowl?

definitions.text: Did it chew up the fowl?

indicators.note: chewing something up mangles it, so the bird's letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Was a predator responsible for eating the chicken?
explanation.definitionFit: A wild canine predator that raids poultry and gobbles greedily.

clue.text: Shilling price label, or should it be a buck?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for shilling, an old British coin
a tag is a label showing a price

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether a price ticket should read a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like a dollar, but means a male deer; a shilling was an old British coin worth one-twentieth of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer is a buck.

clue.text: Lost sheep must have returned to make the argument stick

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
having returned is being back at home

explanation.surface: A stray sheep must come back for the point to be won.
explanation.definitionFit: To press a point forcefully until it is accepted.

clue.text: Hostile to information describing a vaccine

parts.note: anti means against or hostile to
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to data describes an immunisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaccines work by introducing a substance that provokes the body to make antibodies.

clue.text: Cargo list is clearly displayed

definitions.meaning: a ship's document listing its freight
plain to see, obvious

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's freight inventory bears this name, and the adjective means obvious.

clue.text: Jeannie sounds a spirited servant

indicators.note: sounds says the girl's name is heard as a word with another spelling

parts.note: a girl's name, pronounced the same as the lamp spirit

explanation.surface: A girl called Jeannie seems a lively maid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirited' means being a spirit, not lively: the lamp-dwelling slave of Aladdin's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinn in Arabian tales is bound to serve whoever holds its lamp.
